q: I'm also going through a lot personally right now, so by the end of the day I'm completely exhausted and bedtime feels like the hardest part
cx: Two-and-a-half-year-old takes forever at bedtime despite a consistent routine.

q: his dad and i separated about five days ago, and his dad used to do his whole bedtime routine every night. since then i've been doing bedtime by myself, so i'm wondering if the sudden change is what's making him fight sleep so much right now.
cx: Explains the change behind the bedtime fight; the parent who did bedtime has left.

q: i think the nap might be part of the problem because some days he sleeps longer than 2 hours. i'm definitely going to try capping it and seeing if that makes bedtime easier.
cx: Takes a commenter's nap-cap suggestion.

q: Then we went away on a trip to see overseas family for two months and there were no curtains in our room, we shared a room, and it was very hot. Routine was a bit out the window. Any semblance of a sleep schedule crumbled and now we are back home and two months in - it’s just getting worse.
cx: Breastfed 10-month-old had a decent routine at 6 months until a long trip.

q: My daughter for lack of a better word is a screamer. She works herself into an absolute state when she wakes up, day or night.
cx: Describes a baby who wakes hysterical every time.

q: Should I try a sleep training method? Ferber? Pick up put down? Camping out? Will these even work for a hysterical baby?
cx: Wakes every 30 minutes to 3 hours; asks which method fits.

q: I don’t want to get my hopes up, but yesterday we started the new nap schedule you suggested with longer wake windows and less overall sleep and we only had one wake up the whole night. I genuinely feel like a new human today.
cx: Day after a commenter's longer-wake-window schedule; one waking only.

q: Every night I darken the room, turn on white noise, and prewarm his sleeping space with a heating pad. The only reliable way to get him to sleep is nursing so I do. He refuses all pacifiers. I wait until he’s in a deep sleep. I put him down slowly, toes then butt then head
cx: First-time mother, six-week-old who will not stay down anywhere.

q: I do ALL OF THE THINGS. And yet he wakes up within 10 minutes every time. We’ve also done the Snoo with no luck.
cx: After listing every put-down trick.

q: I know the ideal recommendation is taking shifts but as wonderful as my husband has been, he has little to no patience with the crying and I get very nervous about leaving him and the baby alone for hours. He gives me one 3 hours stretch in the afternoon usually. We don’t have family or friends nearby.
cx: Why shift-taking does not work for her; no local help.

q: I hope this is fairly easy to understand 🤦🏻‍♀️ it’s a lot of info but I’m at a loss. What could be causing the short naps, middle of the night wakes and the early morning wakes??
cx: 14-month-old sleep trained at 5 months; two weeks of everything unravelling at once.

q: My wife isn't thrilled about this as she feels it's a "crutch" for him and we should just wait out whatever phase he's going through.
cx: Father found rubbing the child's temple gets sleep in minutes; child is 3.5.

q: Last night he was awake from 2am - 5am....so today will be a fun work day....
cx: Spoke too soon about wakings lessening.

q: The story starts how they often do: My child was a wonderful sleeper from just a couple months old, would fall asleep independently and sleep soundly all night in her own room, and then BAM it all quickly regressed to pure nighttime hell.
cx: Mother of a near-5 and a 2.5-year-old.

q: It’s hours of screaming and fighting every night. We try so hard to hold firm on boundaries….
cx: Toddler refuses bed, floor and room; meltdowns unless mum does bedtime.

q: Poor guy hasn’t been able to sleep in his own bed lately because it’s right across the hall. Tonight he even asked “can i go to sleep at normal bedtime?”
cx: The older sibling's nights are wrecked by the toddler's bedtime.

q: the whole “keep a consistent routine, calmly hold firm boundaries and tell them it’s bedtime and put them back into bed” thing…either those sleep experts have never met a toddler or my toddler is her own unique species.
cx: After weeks of nightly battles; tempted to let her into the parents' bed.

q: At this point though, we’re weighing if it’s worth it for our sanity and sleep for our son.
cx: Weighing lying with her until asleep despite agreeing it is not ideal.

q: I appreciate the input, but it is too early to drop her nap. Her wake windows are age appropriate.
cx: Pushes back on a commenter's drop-the-nap reply.

q: my daughter has NEVER been a good sleeper. she’s been in a sleep regression since the day she was born.
cx: 23-month-old fights bedtime every night.

q: Her pediatrician told me to stop breastfeeding her overnight as she was waking for it for no reason. so i stopped. she maybe slept well like 2 nights and then began waking up the same amount of times as before
cx: Night-weaned on the doctor's advice; it lasted two nights.

q: her pediatrician is useless and just tells me that it’s how she is.
cx: Mother back at work since 13 months; nothing has worked.

q: tried sleep training her but the crying would make her vomit so didn’t continue.
cx: Why she stopped sleep training.

q: It’s now been a week that he will cry up to 20-30 minutes inconsolably push me away and look for his father but then doesn’t even stop crying with him until we give him a bottle. He’s now having 2-3 bottles a night. His wake up time is 5:30am so that’s exhausting in itself. When does this get better?
cx: Baby turned one yesterday; multiple wakings back after improvement.
